clue.text: People on the edge become service men

definitions.meaning: read playfully, those who stand on the verge or border of something
church officials who look after the building and lead processions at services

explanation.surface: Some marginal figures turn into men who work at church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People on the edge' is a whimsical reading: if a verge is an edge, then those on it are the ones in the answer. 'become' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger is a church caretaker who attends at services, and the word also jokingly suggests someone standing on a verge.

clue.text: Truman, with clever lob, destroyed the backbone

indicators.note: the letters of the named words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: President Truman, with a smart lob, wrecked someone's spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' shuffles TRUMAN and CLEVER LOB together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is the column of vertebrae, the anatomical name for the backbone.

clue.text: This guy is well off with an article on the way

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of the road, above it

parts.note: rich means well off
a is the indefinite article
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A man is prosperous, with an article written about him on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This guy' points at a man's name, a fair definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard is a man's name, so it names a particular guy.

clue.text: Settled in fine, in the end

indicators.note: the word for a penalty goes inside the word for the end

parts.note: end as a synonym of itself, the finish
a sconce, in old Oxford usage, is a fine or forfeit, often a tankard of ale

explanation.surface: Settled into the area in the end, all fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fine' sense of the penalty word is old Oxford college slang, a forfeit for breaking table etiquette; 'in' (the second one) puts it inside the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ensconced is established comfortably in a place, nestled there.

clue.text: Flight attendant and cook with a rugged exterior

parts.note: to stew is to cook slowly

indicators.note: only the outside letters of rugged are used, first and last

explanation.surface: A cabin crew member and a chef, both with a rough appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is a cabin attendant on an aircraft or ship.

clue.text: Old currency that was elaborate

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old
the pound is Britain's unit of currency

explanation.surface: A remark about a former coinage that was once elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' looks like an adjective describing the money, but it is a verb meaning to explain at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on a point is to set it out in detail, which is to expound it.

clue.text: Once they ran eagerly, making early starts — being fanatical

parts.note: ex means former, what once was

indicators.note: the opening letters of the five words before it are taken

explanation.surface: Runners once set off eagerly at dawn, as zealots do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early starts' sounds like dawn runs; 'starts' is the signal to take the first letters of they ran eagerly making early.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme views are radical ones, the kind held by a zealot.

clue.text: Instrument that's played softly

definitions.meaning: a keyboard instrument with hammers and strings
the Italian musical direction for performing quietly

explanation.surface: A keyboard that is played quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: The keyboard's name is short for pianoforte, soft-loud; on its own the Italian word is the marking for soft playing.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard instrument shares its name with the musical direction meaning quietly.

clue.text: Nuclear explosion not easily explained

indicators.note: the word nuclear is blown apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A nuclear blast whose cause remains mysterious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something murky or obscure is hard to account for or understand.

clue.text: Cool story from a cousin twice removed, say

parts.note: cool in manner means aloof or distant
a relation is an account or narrative, a story

explanation.surface: A frosty tale told by a far-off member of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' is the older sense of relation, a telling or narration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin twice removed is an example of a far-off family member, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Nations need experts after the end of war

indicators.note: the experts are placed following the letter taken from war
the final letter of the word war is the one wanted

parts.note: aces are experts, top performers

explanation.surface: Countries need skilled people once a war is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Races in the older sense are peoples or nations sharing descent.

clue.text: Charms with appearances on stage

definitions.meaning: a verb, to enchant or delight
the moments when actors walk on in a play

explanation.surface: An actor bewitches the audience each time they come on.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: stress on the second syllable for charming, on the first for comings-on.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral someone is one sense; an actor's comings-on during a performance are the other.

clue.text: English v Australian? Speak quietly at first and disappear

indicators.note: the soft marking is placed before the speaking word rather than after it

parts.note: v as written, the letter of versus
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: In an England versus Australia match, someone talks softly before vanishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English v Australian' reads like a sporting fixture; each word just gives an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that evaporates turns to vapour and vanishes, so the verb can mean simply to vanish.

clue.text: Inwardly copes with artists finding work in the theatre

indicators.note: only the inside letters of copes are taken, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for artists

explanation.surface: A performer manages alongside other artists by getting a stage job.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic musical work performed in a theatre.

clue.text: Cut the grass, protecting tops of daisies under cover

indicators.note: the reed surrounds the other letters, sheltering them

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: Mow the lawn while keeping the flower heads shielded beneath a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops of' applies to three words, not just daisies: D, U and C go inside REED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut back has been reduced, made smaller.

clue.text: Passage — but not around the end of September

indicators.note: the word for excluding is wrapped about the single letter

parts.note: except means but not, excluding

indicators.note: the last letter of September is taken

explanation.surface: A piece of writing that excludes the final part of September.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a longer text.

clue.text: Restrict the arguments against school

parts.note: cons are reasons against, as in pros and cons
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Curb the case being made against a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to limit or hold back, which is to restrict.

clue.text: Clean less than half of lawn for a start

indicators.note: the half-word goes at the front, before the other piece
the first two of the four letters of lawn are wanted

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten

explanation.surface: Tidy up just part of the lawn to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than half' wants to be read together as a fraction; split it after 'than', so the half of lawn stands on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash them, so the verb means to clean.

clue.text: The oily manner required for topless role

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a role is removed

parts.note: a function is a role or purpose

explanation.surface: A slippery manner is needed to land a part with no top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless role' suggests a racy acting part; it means FUNCTION with its first letter lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction can mean a smarmy, ingratiating earnestness, a greasy charm.

clue.text: Cancels material prior to distress sale

indicators.note: the fabric comes before the rearranged letters

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery

indicators.note: a distress sale is a forced one; here the word mangles the letters of sale

explanation.surface: Cloth is written off before a forced clearance sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress sale' is a real phrase for a forced sale; 'distress' is the anagram signal, turning SALE into EALS.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke it, so the verb means cancels.

clue.text: Charge crew with assignation

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
an assignation is an arranged meeting, a date

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is sent out on a secret rendezvous.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official command or instruction, which is a charge given to someone.

clue.text: Model gent (single) with family

parts.note: a gent is a man
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
kin are relatives, family

explanation.surface: A dummy of a single gentleman with his family.
explanation.definitionFit: A manikin is a jointed figure used by artists as a model of the human body.

clue.text: Siding with gangster and not telling the truth

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster
lying means not telling the truth

explanation.surface: Taking the part of a mobster who is also a liar.
explanation.definitionFit: Allying oneself with someone is taking their part, joining their side.

clue.text: Very large vehicle gets award for performance

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very large
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A huge vehicle wins a prize for its showing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette for film acting is known by this name.

clue.text: Right way up (of the kidney)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A medical note: right way up for the kidney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right way up' reads as an orientation instruction, but in a down clue 'up' turns the way word round, giving ENAL after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective renal describes anything relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Nat's into Spanish dish — it could be smoked

indicators.note: Nat is placed within the Spanish dish

parts.note: paella is the saffron rice dish of Spain
the name Nat taken as written; the 's is a contraction of is

explanation.surface: Nat is keen on paella, which might be served smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nat's into' reads as Nat liking the dish, but it is an instruction to put the name inside the rice dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin cigar, something one smokes.

clue.text: Raise, after marriage, is standard

indicators.note: the word for raise is set after the marriage word

parts.note: a union is a marriage
to jack up a car is to raise it

explanation.surface: Lifting things after a wedding is normal practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like an adjective meaning normal; here it is a flag, the British national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Excuse for a party that finished with one

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An excuse for a party that ended with a single guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim to have been elsewhere at the time is a standard excuse.

clue.text: Puzzle in French not an advantage

parts.note: non is French for not
a plus is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: A French phrase for 'not an advantage' is itself a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex or baffle them, which is to puzzle them.

clue.text: Not a horse performing is in shape

parts.note: no means not a, as in no fool
a nag is an old horse
on means performing, as an act on stage

explanation.surface: No horse is putting on a show in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shape' suggests fitness; 'shape' alone is the definition, a nine-sided figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a nine-sided polygon, a geometric figure.
